name: Auth0
description: Auth0 is an identity platform for adding authentication and authorization to web, mobile, B2B, and AI-enabled applications. Buyers should compare MAU-based pricing, organization limits, MFA entitlements, enterprise connections, and migration requirements before committing.
best_for: Development teams that want a managed customer-identity layer with SDKs, Universal Login, social or enterprise connections, Organizations, MFA, and extensibility without building the full identity stack themselves.
features: Auth0 for AI Agents (async authorization, RAG pipeline controls)

alternatives.name: Okta
alternatives.description: Auth0's parent-company workforce identity platform, providing SSO and adaptive MFA for employees/partners across 8,000+ integrations.
alternatives.best_for: Enterprises managing internal workforce access rather than embedding customer-facing auth into an app.

alternatives.name: 1Password
alternatives.description: Provides a credential vault and secrets management platform rather than a developer authentication API.
alternatives.best_for: Teams needing a shared vault for passwords/secrets rather than building login flows into their own product.

pricing.starting_price: Free up to 25,000 MAU; paid self-service starts at $35/month for Essentials at 500 MAU (B2C monthly)

tiers.name: Free
tiers.notes: Up to 25,000 monthly active users; 5 Organizations, 1 Enterprise Connection, 1 custom domain, passwordless authentication, SCIM and community support are listed on the current B2C pricing page.

tiers.name: Essentials
tiers.notes: Shown at $35/month for up to 500 MAU in the B2C monthly view; adds higher limits, Pro MFA, 10 Organizations, log streaming, separate production/development environments and standard support.

tiers.name: Professional
tiers.notes: Shown at $240/month for up to 500 MAU in the B2C monthly view; adds custom database connections, Enterprise MFA and enhanced attack protection. M2M tokens are an add-on.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.notes: Contact sales; custom user and SSO tiers, 99.99% SLA, enterprise rate limits and advanced support/features.

cons: Paid self-service pricing scales with monthly active users and use case, so the displayed $35 Essentials and $240 Professional rates are not universal prices for larger deployments.

Plan entitlements differ sharply: Pro MFA starts on Essentials, Enterprise MFA and custom database connections start on Professional, while some advanced security and administration capabilities remain Enterprise-only or add-ons.

B2B identity can change the plan decision: Auth0 notes that Enterprise Connections, Self-Service SSO, and SCIM entitlements differ by use case and may require moving to B2B plans rather than staying on the B2C self-service tiers.
The Free tier is generous on MAU but has tighter operational limits, including 5 Organizations, 1 Enterprise Connection, 3 admin/contributor seats and 1 day of log retention.
